HOLIDAY EDITION · 2026
Keep this handy

Before you buy
the airplane thing.

Four small checks that make a gift easier to get right.

  1. Find the personal connection. Their first airplane, favorite airshow, or an item they actually asked for.
  2. Check the fit. Aircraft plugs, tablet models, clothing sizes and shelf space all matter.
  3. Check the delivered total. Include tax and shipping, then read the delivery estimate and return terms.
  4. Keep technical gifts collaborative. For headsets and cockpit equipment, let the pilot choose the exact version.

Questions you can ask without ruining the surprise

  • What airplane did you first learn in?
  • Is there anything in your flight bag you wish you could replace?
  • Do you have a wishlist link with the exact version selected?
  • What tablet and case do you use?
  • Would you rather choose equipment together or get a surprise for home?

A note for partners and family

You do not need to learn every piece of aviation terminology. An exact product link is more useful than a vague model name. If you cannot check compatibility without giving away the surprise, choose an off-duty gift with a personal connection, such as their favorite aircraft model or a small airshow keepsake.

For holiday delivery

Use the destination-specific arrival estimate at checkout. A dispatch date is not an arrival guarantee. Keep the receipt and any gift-card redemption details secure. For personalized items, confirm the spelling and review the return policy before payment.
